title: arctostaphylos hookeri subsp. franciscana
intro: Arctostaphylos hookeri subsp. franciscana, commonly known as the Franciscan manzanita, is a type of shrub that belongs to the heath family (Ericaceae). It is native to the coastal mountains of central and southern California, where it grows in the wild. The plant is rich in health benefits, including its ability to boost the immune system and reduce inflammation due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The bioactive constituents of Arctostaphylos hookeri subsp. franciscana include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as antimicrobial, antiviral, and antifungal activities.
